name: TX-37
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+30 partisan lean makes a Democratic loss structurally unlikely
Casar holds a roughly ten-to-one fundraising advantage and over $550,000 on hand versus about $2,600 for Pena
Prediction markets price Casar's reelection near 97 percent
No public polls or outside spending signal any competitive race
model.rationale: The forecast rests on the district's strong Democratic lean plus Casar's overwhelming financial edge, with markets pricing his reelection near certainty and no polling or spending suggesting a contest. The margin stays close to the fundamentals-based estimate, tempered slightly by the total absence of survey data.
model.watch: Any late independent spending against Casar or a surprise poll showing a single-digit race would warrant revisiting the forecast.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Texas's 37th District, anchored in Austin, is one of the most Democratic-leaning seats in the state, with a partisan lean of roughly 30 points. Representative Greg Casar is seeking reelection with the advantages of incumbency and a decisive financial edge. He has raised about $1.37 million and holds more than $550,000 on hand, while Republican nominee Lauren Pena has raised roughly $130,000 and reported only about $2,600 in cash. No outside groups are spending in the race.

No public general-election polls are available, and national race raters have not flagged the contest as competitive. Prediction markets price Casar's chances at about 97 percent. The forecast expects Casar to win by a wide margin, around 28 points, with the main uncertainty stemming from the lack of polling rather than any evidence of a genuine contest.
